transcript_or_text: I'm a board certified PA and I think a lot about what medical conditions or types of people would benefit from an infrared sauna. One area I found particularly interesting was rheumatology. There's some early research showing infrared sauna can temporarily improve pain and stiffness in people with rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory conditions. My wife actually has RA and lupus and heat has always been something she responds really well to. It feels great in her joints and there's emerging research looking at how whole body heat exposure may influence inflammatory and cardiovascular pathways. And beyond rheumatologic conditions there's research looking at sauna therapy for cardiovascular health, exercise recovery, chronic pain, and overall well-being. Now this isn't a treatment for RA or lupus and I wouldn't replace medication with a sauna but as a potential adjunct to a healthy lifestyle the research is pretty interesting and that's honestly what makes a sauna like Peak so interesting to me. Not just as a place to relax but it's something that could potentially become part of a consistent wellness and recovery routine.
